text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam's newly elected National Assembly is the most educated in history, and has its greatest ever representation of women and ethnic minority groups.

-- The inability of local enterprises to expand their overseas markets, a limited domestic consumer base, backward technology and equipment, a lack of capital and wide-spread smuggling are causing set-backs for the industrial sector.
-- Vietnam Post and Telecommunication Corporation has signed three deals worth $900 million with British, French, and Japanese firms to develop the telephone networks in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.
-- Ho Chi Minh City plans to build a $79.8 million underground carpark in the city's downtown area.
-- Vietnam Maritime Bank plans to sell 30 percent of shares totalling $6.95 million to increase its registered capital to $21.4 million.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has asked the southern province of Ba Ria-Vung Tau to reorganise the oil service system to make it more competitive and to prepare conditions to form an international maritime service.
-- A drug trafficker has been sentenced to death by a local people's court in the northern province of Lang Son.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has signed a document outlining instructions for reinforcing security in oil exploitation.
-- Water levels in the Mekong River catchment area have been rising, causing at least 2,000 hectares of paddy in southern Long An province to be submerged.
